name: Why does my toilet overflow when I flush?

mainEntity.name: Why does my toilet overflow when I flush?

acceptedAnswer.text: A toilet typically overflows during flushing due to a clog in the drainpipe or the toilet trap. When water can't flow down freely, it backs up and spills over the bowl's rim. Common culprits include excessive toilet paper, non-flushable items like wipes or feminine hygiene products, or a blocked vent pipe. Less commonly, a malfunctioning fill valve can cause the tank to overfill, leading to an overflow.
acceptedAnswer.description: Toilet overflows during flushing are usually caused by a clog in the drainpipe or toilet trap, preventing water from flowing down.
